findings: Primary source preserves only the requirement to handwrite a singly linked-list structure with CRUD; language, API shape, index-versus-value semantics, null policy, and tail-pointer policy are not preserved constraints.
Candidate clearly labels Java generics, index-based CRUD, null support, and tail tracking as answer-side assumptions rather than source facts.
The representation invariant is explicit and the CRUD pointer updates, index bounds, and head/tail transitions are internally consistent.
Candidate Java compiles with warnings treated as errors and an independent 10000-operation ArrayList differential harness passes empty, single-node, head/middle/tail, null, and out-of-bounds cases.
Complexity claims match the implementation: tail append and head insert/remove are constant time while index-based traversal operations are linear in the worst case.
No fabricated production experience or placeholder implementation was found; follow-ups are specific to the linked-list contract and include failure/boundary cases.
